messages:
Maya (People Ops): Quick ask  we'd like to run a small global micro-spot awards pilot for two weeks in July. Physical kiosks in SF/NY + digital redemptions for remote folks and EMEA/APAC. Need clarity on payroll/tax treatement and a pragmatic ops flow. Who can advise? :globe_with_meridians:
Tomas (Payroll): High level: US taxable if gifts > $50 per employee per year. For small one-off e-gifts under $50 it's usually de minimis, but we need to track redemptions per person across the year. For EMEA it's country-dependent (UK treats most vouchers as earnings). We should cap per-person redemptions and treat any overage as taxable with proper reporting.
Emi (Benefits): Also consider vendor method: if vendor issues e-gift cards directly to employees (not paid through payroll), we still need to capture value for benefits reporting in some countries. Better to treat everything via our vendor PO and keep a redemption log.
Raj (EMEA Ops): For UK and Germany, small vouchers under ~50 GBP/EUR are usually fine but mandatory reporting can still apply — we'd prefer to issue digital swag (stickers, recognition certificate) for EMEA and e-gift cards only in approved markets. Happy to maintain a per-country whitelist.
Zoe (People Ops): Operational proposal:
1) Pilot length: July 6-17 (10 business days).
2) Per-person cap: $40 USD equivalent across pilot window.
3) Remote redemptions: Slack DM with single-use QR/eCode. Physical kiosks will accept QR codes or printed token cards.
4) Vendor: single PO to vendor + vendor invoice.
Can we get buy-in on the cap and whitelist approach?
Tomas (Payroll): Cap is fine. Need a redemption sheet with employee ID + email + amount for payroll reconciliation. Also include country code to apply local rules. I can supply a CSV template:
```
employee_id, email, country_code, amount_usd, redemption_ts, voucher_id
```
We'll use this to batch any reporting.
Maya (People Ops): Great  I'll create the sheet and the Google form for kiosks to log redemptions. Zoe can you coordinate ticket/QR generation?
Zoe (People Ops): On it. Plan: pre-generate single-use QR tokens via vendor API, store token->employee mapping encrypted, and send as Slack DM. For kiosks we'll print a small set of physical token cards (10/day/site). We'll rotate serials.
Emi (Benefits): Note on employee experience: include a short message in the DM that explains tax treatment and cap, plus opt-in checkbox for receiving an e-gift card (required for some countries).
Raj (EMEA Ops): I'll draft the country whitelist and upload to the shared doc. Suggest we exclude FR/BE for direct e-gift cards without legal review.
Tomas (Payroll): Two more asks: 1) vendor invoice must include per-item unit price for accounting; 2) keep separate expense code: CULT-SPOT-2026 so we don't mix with normal perks budget.
Maya (People Ops): Will request invoice line-itemization and create the expense code. Also tagging legal: @Noah can you confirm if we need a cross-border vendor addendum?
ops-bot: Legal review recommended for non-US e-gift issuance — guideline: https://drive.internal/policies/global-gifts-guidance.pdf
Maya (People Ops): Thanks. Next steps: Zoe to set up token flow + share sample QR DM text by Friday; Tomas to send CSV template; Raj to upload whitelist; Emi to prepare the DM tax notice copy; I'll get two vendor quotes and estimated pilot budget. If no objections by EOD Friday we'll proceed with procurement. :rocket:
Tomas (Payroll): I'll drop the CSV template and a short reconciliation checklist into the shared folder by EOD.
Zoe (People Ops): Draft QR DM message: "Congrats! You've received a Redwood Micro-Spot. Claim by clicking this single-use link: https://redwood.kudos/claim/XXXX (expires 48h). Max $40 per person for pilot. T&Cs: https://drive.internal/policies/culture-spot-tcs.pdf" Will share token generation demo on Monday.
Raj (EMEA Ops): Whitelist uploaded: UK, DE, NL, IE allowed for e-gift cards. FR/BE ask legal review. Link: https://drive.internal/culture/whitelist_1959003456.csv
Emi (Benefits): Tax notice copy ready. Will put in the DM and the kiosk sign: "Small rewards under $40 may still be taxable in some countries. See details: https://drive.internal/policies/global-gifts-guidance.pdf"
Maya (People Ops): Perfect. I'll collect quotes and post final pilot plan next week. Thanks all for quick turnaround! :heart:
